anomalies.observed: The input reverse-polarity stage uses T8, labeled AON6407, as a series high-side MOSFET. Its gate is fed from the input through R40 (33k) and clamped by D1 (12V) to GND. AON6407 is an N-channel MOSFET, and this arrangement does not provide the gate voltage above its source needed to turn it on as a high-side switch.
anomalies.expected: The reverse-polarity stage should use a suitably driven high-side MOSFET arrangement, such as a P-channel MOSFET or an N-channel device with a proper gate driver, so the 24 V rail passes normally while reverse polarity is blocked.

evidence.quote: Reverse polarity protection; T8 AON6407; R40 33k; D1 12V; page 1
README states the board has “reverse polarity protection”

anomalies.impact: The MOSFET is not properly enhanced in normal operation, so the board may receive power only through the MOSFET body diode or may fail to power up; the intended reverse-polarity protection is also not reliably achieved.

anomalies.observed: The schematic shows PR6 labeled LiDAR connected through H12: its supply and ground are wired, and its SDA/SCL pins connect to the I2C bus.
anomalies.expected: The specification says the TF-Luna LiDAR is not wired in this revision: its pins are free and it is excluded from the board.

evidence.quote: PR6 LiDAR; H12 pins connect to VCC, NET0081, NET0030 and GND; page 1
PR1 with on_board: no and all four pins typed free — it is not connected to any net

anomalies.impact: The build adds a powered I2C LiDAR device that the specified design does not include, changing the sensor interface and potentially adding bus loading or device-address conflicts.

parsed.summary: An anomaly is present: the high-side reverse-polarity stage uses an N-channel MOSFET without a suitable gate drive. The schematic also wires a LiDAR sensor that the specification says should be unconnected and excluded.
